#  1. aaa      ACCESS     different: the TACACS+ primary host is 192.0.2.42 (the device has:
#                         192.0.2.99) (tacacs primary 192.0.2.42). Fixed by step 3.
#  2. aaa      ACCESS     missing: the TACACS+ secret word (tacacs secret <secret>). Fixed by step 2.
#  3. snmp     MONITORING different: the SNMP read-only community (the device has: another string)
#                         (snmp ro-community <secret:1>). Fixed by step 1.
# Consistent: mgmt-acl. Not planned: breakglass (walkthrough Step 10).
# Secrets are not typed by this output: a secret step names the command that shows its value (tacctl
# scope secret show lab, tacctl scope snmp lab show --reveal), and --secrets puts the value in the
# step.
# Note: tacacs default-services: the unit allows more services than the standard asks for (serial,
# web, restful-api): kept, not compared.
# Note: the IP tables list ends with the final DROP and the policies of the walkthrough's last step:
# kept, not compared.
# Note: aaa: 13 statements of the device's own, kept on purpose.
# Note: snmp: 4 statements of the device's own, kept on purpose.
# WARNING: Steps 2-3 change what the unit asks of the TACACS+ server or how it answers when the server
# fails: a wrong secret word, host, port or service name does not stop a login, it returns every login
# to the unit's Default User Access level, and Fallback Local decides whether the unit's own accounts
# work when the server does not answer; keep the serial session open and do the check after the ESC
# step before anything else.
# The unit has no commit-confirm and no rollback: every value is live as soon as its Enter is
# accepted, and the configuration is written to flash when a top-level menu is left with ESC (any
# session that leaves one saves everything). tacctl types nothing: you do each step yourself.
# Before you start: keep the serial console, or a second session logged in as an Administrator, open
# until the check at the end passes; type /SN and make sure no other administrator is on the unit (the
# pull saw 1 other session).
# The way back is tacctl device config plan lab-unit --backout: the old values.
#
# Type this first, on lab-unit, and check the version:   /H
# The title must read "COMMAND MENU: Version 8.10": tacctl's tables are those of that command menu,
# and another version may number its pages differently: stop. /J shows the unit's Site ID: the pull
# read wti.site.example.net; another one means this is not the unit.
#
##### DO THESE STEPS ON: lab-unit #####
# At the unit's prompt type /N and Enter. For each step type the item numbers of its second column,
# one at a time with Enter after each, then what the arrow says. A pick: the number of the line
# that reads as shown. ESC goes back one level. A value is live as soon as its Enter is accepted.
#  1. /N  25  7  Read-Only Community   -> <the scope's SNMP community: tacctl scope snmp lab show --reveal>   was: (another string)
#  2. /N  28  4  Secret Word           -> <the scope's TACACS+ secret: tacctl scope secret show lab>   was: (undefined)
#  3. /N  28  2  Primary host/address  -> 1 (IPv4), then 192.0.2.42   was: 192.0.2.99
#  4. ESC ESC  leave /N: wait for "Saving configuration to flash"
#  5. CHECK from a SECOND session (this one stays open): log in as a member of scope lab and type
#      /H; the help lists the commands of the level the server assigned (Step 8 of tacctl config
#      wti). Go on only when it does.
##### END OF STEPS #####
#
# Check now. The unit has no rollback: nothing undoes this by itself.
#   From the tacctl server:   tacctl device config pull lab-unit --diff     (snmp and aaa: ok)
#   In a second session:      log in as a member of scope lab and type /H (the help lists the commands of the assigned level), then /X
#
# To undo it: tacctl device config plan lab-unit --backout (the steps with the values the pull
# showed; tacctl keeps this plan's back-out until the next plan with changes).
# Do not: paste anything outside the banners; paste a block into another unit; leave /N with ESC

# Locked out (the paste cut your session and no login works)? A superuser runs: tacctl breakglass hold lab-unit --reason "..."
